nodes.text: TXN-C13 used token TOK-C13, tokenized from card CRD-C13 issued on account ACC-C13, and the token acted for agent provider AGP-C13 (Voyager Assistant) under mandate MDT-C13. The transaction was USD 780.00, while the mandate capped transactions at USD 600.00 and limited scope to hotel room only; the order includes a USD 180 airport transfer, so the transaction exceeds the mandate terms.

nodes.text: TXN-C13 is a posted USD 780.00 agentic-commerce purchase directly linked to Sable Quay Hotel (US lodging merchant, MCC 7011). The transaction was initiated through Voyager Assistant for customer Nora Okafor using token TOK-C13; the linked PurchaseOrder contains a $600 hotel room and $180 premium airport transfer.

nodes.evidence_path: DSP-2026-90011-[DISPUTES]->TXN-C11-ATO-01-[FROM_DEVICE]->DEV-C11-NEW; TXN-C11-ATO-01-[FROM_IP]->IP-C11-VPN; TXN-C11-ATO-01-[AT_MERCHANT]->MER-C11-AUDIO; AEV-C11-01-[ABOUT]->ACC-C11-01 and AEV-C11-01-[TRIGGERED_BY]->DEV-C11-NEW and AEV-C11-01-[CHANGED_PHONE_TO]->PHN-C11-NEW; DEV-C11-NEW and IP-C11-VPN each link to 40 C11-ATO transactions; MEM-C11-FRIENDLY-[ABOUT]->DSP-2026-90011
nodes.text: The disputed TXN-C11-ATO-01 appears to be part of a coordinated account-takeover campaign, not friendly/household use. Immediately before the purchase, CUS-C11-01 had a phone-change/password-reset event triggered by DEV-C11-NEW; the same new device, hosting/VPN IP and Orbital Audio merchant were then used for 40 ecommerce purchases across 40 distinct C11 accounts over 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-18. This directly contradicts the prior friendly-fraud memory note.

nodes.text: The booking request exceeded the linked mandate: MDT-C13 permits hotel room only up to USD 600 from 2026-09-01 through 2026-10-31, while TXN-C13 is USD 780 and ORD-C13 explicitly includes a prohibited premium airport transfer for USD 180. Voyager Assistant is the evidenced initiator, but the graph does not establish that Nora personally placed the booking beyond authorizing the agent relationship.

nodes.text: For TXN-C13 on 2026-10-16, the graph shows no identifiable customer-side account-takeover or household/authorized-user security signal: CUS-C13 is the sole primary holder of ACC-C13, with no AccountEvent, login, phone/email change, password-reset, customer device/IP, shared-device, or additional authorized-user relationship found. The affirmative explanation is agentic commerce through Voyager Assistant under MDT-C13, with the USD 780 transaction exceeding the mandate's USD 600 hotel-only scope.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.evidence_path: TXN-C13 has no VIA_TERMINAL, FROM_DEVICE, or FROM_IP neighbors; token/customer/provider pivots return no other transactions; CRD-C13 has no COMPROMISED_AT neighbor; global explicit relationship checks return only unrelated CRD-0000001/TRM-0000001 and CUS-0000001/CUS-0000002 pairs.
nodes.text: TXN-C13 is isolated on the requested explicit relationship dimensions: no other transaction shares a FROM_DEVICE, FROM_IP, or VIA_TERMINAL edge with it, and there is no SAME_ACTOR edge linking its identified customer/account to another actor. No COMPROMISED_AT edge exists for CRD-C13. Searches also found no other transaction using TOK-C13, CRD-C13, ACC-C13, AGP-C13, or MER-C13-HOTEL.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: For an AI-agent purchase, when an itemized order separates an in-scope component at or below the mandate cap from a component expressly excluded or above the cap, allocate the in-scope amount as authorized and the excluded/over-cap amount as unauthorized; do not classify the whole transaction as unauthorized solely because the agent exceeded its mandate. Revalidate any later evidence of broader customer approval.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: In agentic payments, distinguish the agentic payment provider/initiator from the merchant. Use the transaction's direct merchant relationship as the operative merchant identity; do not substitute the provider's name absent affirmative descriptor or facilitator evidence.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: A security-change event shortly before disputed activity, combined with the same new device and hosting/VPN IP spanning many accounts in a bounded time window, is a strong coordinated account-takeover signal. It should outweigh an isolated matching-merchant-login theory unless affirmative household or authorized-user evidence supports that alternative.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Absence of device, IP, login, credential-change, authorization, or related-record links is neutral graph evidence: it should not by itself establish either account takeover or customer authorization. Resolve agentic disputes from affirmative mandate, itemization, and actor evidence, while treating missing external audit records as unresolved provenance.
